options.content:
**Hero metric = Trades/sec** — each order fill books a trade to trade-service. The *same* workload produces the *same* fills in both states; the difference is **how fast they clear**:

- **009** (poll / lock / inline-JPA): trades dribble out as a low line over minutes (~single/tens per sec).
- **009b** (LMAX hot path): the same trades clear in a brief, tall spike (sub-second).

Both states use the **same ports**, so run **one at a time** and compare across runs. Grafana is served at `/grafana/` (e.g. `http://localhost:8080/grafana/`).

**Ticks/sec caveat:** for **009b** this is true sequenced input-event throughput (~10k–25k/s). For **009** it is only the **1 Hz scheduled poll** — 009 exposes no per-price-tick counter, so read **Trades/sec** for 009's effective throughput.

**Peak trades/sec** is computed server-side at **250ms** resolution via `max_over_time(...[$__range:250ms])` — step-independent, so it reports the busiest 250ms window in view regardless of panel width. The `order-matcher` scrape job runs at **250ms** to capture the burst; a burst shorter than 250ms is averaged to its 250ms-equivalent.

panels.title: Peak trades booked/sec (sustained)
panels.description: Peak SUSTAINED booking rate — the highest 5s-average rate at which trades are committed to the database (the real bottleneck). On 009b: traderx_trades_persisted_total (projector → Postgres). On 009 (inline JPA): the fill counter, which IS the persist there. Same meaning on both → directly comparable, and DB-bounded so it reflects true throughput, not in-memory burst. (009b's raw matcher burst is still in traderx_trades_per_second_peak.)

panels.title: Trades per second (fills booked)
panels.description: Rate of order fills (each fill = one trade booked to trade-service). 009 = low line over minutes; 009b = brief tall spike. Same total fills in both states. Evaluated at 250ms min-step with linear interpolation so spikes are not visually distorted.

panels.title: Order submits (acks)/sec
panels.description: Rate of accepted order create events (POST /orders).

panels.title: Matcher ticks/sec  (009b: input events · 009: 1 Hz poll)
panels.description: 009b: sequenced input events processed by the BLP (true matcher throughput, ~10k–25k/s under load). 009: scheduled poll cadence only (~1/s) — 009 has no per-price-tick counter, so use Trades/sec for 009's real throughput.
